newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 10.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Carlton president John Elliott yesterday launched an attack against the Australian Football League for appealing against the Supreme Court decision which found in favour of Greg Williams, overturning his nine-week suspension for interfering with an umpire Page 20.

Euroleague team Wigan defeated Canterbury 22-18 at Belmore Sports Ground in last night's round of the Super League World Club Challenge. Wigan led 10-0 at half time and stretched their lead to 22-0 in the 51st minute, but allowed Canterbury to score three tries in the last 15 minutes. The first eight Euroleague teams to contest the competition were beaten. Page 18.

Fremantle coach Gerard Neesham last night accused the umpires of home-team bias against the team, and of contributing to its 15.15.(105) to 12.7.(79) loss to Australian Football League premiers North Melbourne at the Melbourne Cricket Ground yesterday. Nesham said "there was an incredible inconsistency in the interpretations of the rules". Neesham will speak with umpires coach David Levens today to express his concerns. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Wallaby back-rower Willie Ofahengaue has probably played his last international Test for Australia. The 27-Test veteran is under contract to the New South Wales Rugby Union for another season, but with unions considering a trade-off, he may be seen in Engish club colours later this year. Page 45.

Adelaide City veteran Alex Tobin will lead the Socceroos for the first time in a World Cup match when they meet the Solomon Islands tomorrow in their first qualifying match for France 1998. Tobin has 65 international appearances, and beat Spanish-based Auelio Vidmar for the captaincy. Page 45.

New South Wales State of Origin coach Tom Raudonikis called a team meeting yesterday after a training session on Sunday that he described as disgraceful. Raudonikis said the team had become complacent and "everything was coming a bit easy for them", but had put in a better training session yesterday in preparation for tomorrow night's match against Queensland at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. New South Wales is currently one up in the best of three series. Page 45.
THE AGE

Several Ericsson Cup soccer clubs are drafting letters of complaint to the Soccer Australia board alleging a conflict of interest by Australian Socceroo coach Terry Venables. Venables' English first-division club Portsmouth is buying at least two members of the national squad. Venables said there was no conflict of interest in him being chairman of Portsmouth and coach of the Australian national side, and that the Portsmouth manager had made the decision on which players to buy. Page B8.

Prominent racehorse owner Barry Larter yesterday warned his star galloper Alfa would be sent to Randwick to be trained if the dirt surface at Flemington did not improve. Larter said he believed the controversial $2.9 million dirt track at Flemington may have contributed to Alfa's off-fore tendon injury, which he damaged in the Debonair Stakes in February. Page B6.

Hockeyroos player Alyson Annan scored the deciding goal with 11 seconds remaining on Sunday, defeating Germany 2-1 and winning Australia the Champions Trophy for the fourth consecutive time. Twenty-three-year-old Annan received the best goal-getter and best player of the tournament awards. Page B6.
THE HERALD SUN

Queensland State of Origin coach Paul Vautin has ruled out the possibility of including Julian O'Neill in his starting line-up for tomorrow night's second match against New South Wales. O'Neill was selected for the Queensland team after just two matches with his new Australian Rugby League team South Sydney, which he joined after being cut from Super League team Perth for disciplinary reasons last month. Page 75.

Australian 500cc motorcycle world champion Michael Doohan yesterday called for a change in race starting rules after he became confused at the beginning of the French Grand Prix on the weekend. Doohan was placed sixth after the first lap despite starting in pole position. He had hesitated when the green start light went out to signal the start of the race, but came on again moments later, going on to win the race. Page 70.

St Kilda officials have vowed to stand firm over their star player Nicky Winmar, who was dropped from the Saints team that defeated West Coast on Sunday after he missed a compulsory training session on Friday night. Saints chief executive Don Hanly said Winmar was expected at training this week. Winmar's manager claims he was having treatment for tears to a hamstring, and was experiencing personal problems. Page 78.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The Australian Jockey Club is expected to abandon its push to have night racing at Randwick and to endorse Canterbury racecourse instead as Sydney's night racing venue at a meeting on Friday, following weeks of contention over which venue should be given approval. Sydney Turf Club chairman Ralph Lucas expects Canterbury will be approved as the venue when the two clubs meet next week. Page 62.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker has confirmed he will reject a demand from Gold Coast players for an assurance their club will be included in the 1998 competition. Whittaker said the ARL could not give any of the clubs an assurance.Page 57.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb finished six strokes behind American Pat Hurst in the LPGA Oldsmobile classic in Michigan yesterday, despite hitting a four-under-par 68 in the final round to finish at three-under 285. Page 54.
